text_blocks.snippet: Derek Carr, the former New Orleans Saints quarterback, has retired due to a shoulder injury. He announced his retirement on May 10, 2025, after an 11-year NFL career. The injury, a labral tear and significant degenerative changes to his rotator cuff, was discovered through medical scans.

Carr's retirement decision came after considering surgery, which would have sidelined him for the entire 2025 season, and trying to play through the injury with injections and rehabilitation. Ultimately, he decided that neither option was viable for him to return to 100%.

The injury occurred during a Week 14 game against the New York Giants where he was scrambling for a first down. He landed awkwardly, bracing the fall with his left wrist and seemingly injuring his right shoulder. While he initially cleared concussion protocol, the shoulder injury was later confirmed.
